text.p: A conference of foreign ministers from 27 European and Mediterranean countries closed five hours late on Wednesday because of a dispute over the Middle East part of the final statement.

Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo declared the two-day meeting closed at 5.15 p.m. (1515 GMT) after a brief ceremony in the Maltese capital Valletta. The ceremony was originally scheduled to start at 12 noon (1000 GMT).
The final text on the Middle East was not immediately available but Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said it endorsed the principle of "land for peace" in the Middle East.
A text circulated shortly before had deleted this reference, diluting the text in the eyes of the Arab states.
This text said the ministers expressed "deep concern about the obstacles which are blocking the Middle East peace process.
"(They stressed) the need for a just, comprehensive and lasting settlement in the Middle East, within the framework of the peace process as agreed in Madrid on 31 October, 1991," the text said.
"We had a major political problem -- the question of how to fit the Middle East into the Malta declaration," van Mierlo said, explaining the delay.
